landmarks.name: Lake Mendota
landmarks.character: The big one: 9,740 acres (39.4 km2), max depth 83 ft (25.3 m), mean 42 ft, ~21.6 mi of shoreline, 500 million m3 of water, surface elevation ~850 ft, 4.5-year residence time. Max length 5.6 mi, max width 4.1 mi. The 'deep hole' sits between Picnic Point and Maple Bluff. Northernmost, largest and deepest lake of the chain; Ho-Chunk name Waaksikhomikra. Eutrophic since late-1800s farm runoff; zebra mussels reproducing since 2015. ~34 fish species: walleye, musky, northern pike, white bass, yellow perch, largemouth and smallmouth bass. Inflows from west to east: Pheasant Branch Creek, Dorn Creek, Sixmile Creek, Yahara River, Token Creek; single outflow is the Yahara at Tenney. Median ice duration 105 days, average freeze ~Dec 20, longest ice on record 161 days (1880-81), shortest ~3 weeks (2001-02); record kept since 1852-53 and the lake has lost ~6 weeks of ice over that span. Huge fetch means real waves and a genuine wind system.
landmarks.game_idea: The overworld's OCEAN — the one body of water big enough that crossing it is a decision, not a step. Gate it behind a traversal item. Wind is a live vector field blowing down the long NE-SW axis: sailing with it is fast, against it forces tacking (zig-zag input puzzle). The 'deep hole' between Picnic Point and Maple Bluff is the single dive-only dungeon entrance — a drowned limnology station. Ice season converts the whole surface into a walkable overworld tier with a 105-day timer.

landmarks.name: Picnic Point
landmarks.character: A narrow wooded peninsula reaching nearly 1 mile (1.6 km) into Lake Mendota from the UW campus, the signature finger on the map. Gravel trail runs the spine; 1 mi entrance-to-tip, 2 mi round trip. Archaeological evidence of habitation spanning at least 12,000 years; UW acquired it in 1941. Part of the 300-acre Lakeshore Nature Preserve that covers 4 miles of Mendota's south shore. Fire circles at the tip are currently closed to the public. Walkable end to end, no vehicles.
landmarks.game_idea: The tutorial peninsula and the map's most legible silhouette. Linear one-way-in, one-way-out corridor: perfect for a first dungeon-adjacent gauntlet where the player cannot flee sideways. The narrow neck near the base is a natural gate/checkpoint. From the tip, a Whirlpool/warp node launches you across open water to Governor's Island — the first time the player crosses the big lake instead of walking around it. Twelve millennia of occupation justifies stacked archaeological strata as a vertical mini-dungeon.

landmarks.name: Second Point Woods
landmarks.character: The next headland west of Picnic Point inside the Lakeshore Nature Preserve. Originally small red oak groves marooned in farmland; the surrounding fields have regenerated since the mid-20th century, leaving a visible hard edge between old-growth oak and young successional woods. Reached on foot via the Lakeshore Path; adjacent to Frautschi Point, Raymer's Cove, Garrett's Cove, Angler's Cove, Bill's Woods and Eagle Heights Woods (28 acres of bluff-top with three Native American burial mounds at the high point).
landmarks.game_idea: A visible seam in the world: two forest tilesets meeting along a dead-straight line, because that line is a 19th-century fence row. Make it literal — old-growth side has ancient enemies and mound guardians, regrowth side is younger and safer. The line itself is the puzzle: follow the boundary to find the buried surveyor's marker. Eagle Heights bluff is the high-vantage point that reveals the full lake map when climbed.

landmarks.name: Governor's Island
landmarks.character: A 60-acre teardrop peninsula on Mendota's north shore — an actual island until the 1860s, when a narrow causeway tied it to the mainland. Named for Governor Leonard J. Farwell, who owned it until 1858 and donated it and adjacent land to the state for the first State Hospital for the Insane; the grounds now hold Mendota Mental Health Institute. Notable exposed sandstone rock outcrop on the shore — a rarity on these lakes. Heavily used by dog walkers and birders. Walkable, but it sits on hospital grounds.
landmarks.game_idea: An island that stopped being an island — the causeway is a man-made land bridge you can sever or restore, flipping the location between 'walk there' and 'must Surf there' and changing which enemies and items are reachable. The institution grounds give you a legitimately eerie, gated, rule-bound interior zone without inventing anything. The sandstone outcrop is the one climbable/breakable cliff face on the north shore — Rock Smash / Waterfall anchor.

landmarks.name: Lake Monona
landmarks.character: 3,274 acres (13.25 km2), mean depth 27 ft, max depth 74 ft (some sources 64 ft), ~28 billion gallons, ~13 mi of shoreline of which about 40% is publicly owned, elevation ~845 ft — roughly 5 ft below Mendota. Residence time ~1.1 years (9.5 months by one measure); freezes about 107 days a year. Inflows: Yahara River, Starkweather Creek, Wingra Creek. Ho-Chunk name Tchee-ho-bo-kee-xa-te-la, 'Teepee Lake'; 'Monona' glossed as beautiful. Fish: bluegill and panfish, largemouth and smallmouth bass, musky, northern pike, walleye, lake sturgeon. Otis Redding's plane crashed into it on Dec 10, 1967. Level is regulated by the locks at Mendota's Yahara outlet — Monona is the downstream lake in a plumbed system.
landmarks.game_idea: The second, tamer sea — smaller, warmer, weedier, ringed by city. Where Mendota is wind and depth, Monona is traffic and structure: causeways, a convention-center roof, seawalls. Because its level is set by the Tenney lock upstream, make water level a PLAYER-CONTROLLED GLOBAL VARIABLE: raise it to float over barriers, drop it to expose lakebed passages and the 1967 wreck. One lever, whole-lake consequences.

landmarks.name: Monona Bay
landmarks.character: The squared-off northwest lobe of Lake Monona, nearly cut off from the main lake by the John Nolen Drive causeway and the rail embankment — effectively a walled-in pond with a narrow opening. Ringed by the Capital City Trail and the Lake Monona Loop (a ~13-mile signed shoreline route). Wingra Creek enters at its southwest corner. Downtown Madison and the Capitol rise directly behind it. Currently disrupted by John Nolen Dr. reconstruction (2025-2027), with a 2.6-mile marked detour around the bay and a planned dock and overlook near Olin Park.
landmarks.game_idea: A near-enclosed starter harbor: safe water where the player learns Surf before being allowed onto open Monona. The causeway is a wall with a single gap — a chokepoint you can block, guard, or gate with a toll. Ideal for a boat-rental hub, a fishing minigame, and a slow, circumnavigable shore path. The active construction gives you a canonical excuse for a rerouted, half-built section that changes between visits.

landmarks.name: Wicawak Bay (formerly Squaw Bay)
landmarks.character: Small bay at Lake Monona's southeastern corner. Renamed by unanimous Dane County Board vote in September 2019 from a slur to Wicawak, the Ho-Chunk word for muskrat — a name the Ho-Chunk Nation first proposed in 2005, honoring both their history as fur trappers and the muskrat's standing in Ho-Chunk tradition. Not yet indexed under the new name in OpenStreetMap.
landmarks.game_idea: A quiet corner-of-the-map bay with a muskrat motif: burrowing lodge NPCs, a dive-and-tunnel puzzle through submerged reed lodges, muskrat-themed catchable creature. Handle the naming respectfully and make it a story beat — an old sign, a new sign, and an NPC who explains why the map you're carrying is out of date. A named-thing-can-be-renamed mechanic is a genuinely good quest hook.

landmarks.name: Lake Wingra
landmarks.character: The little one: 1.3 km2 (~345 acres impounded), mean depth 9 ft, max depth just 14 ft (4.3 m), ~4 mi (5.9 km) of shoreline, frozen ~120 days a year — longest ice season of the group because it is shallowest. Spring-fed: Big Spring, White Clay Spring (686 ft east of Big Spring), West Spring, and the Council Ring / Marston springs cluster (Council Spring averages 221 gal/min) rise in the UW Arboretum on the south and west shores; only a fraction of the historical springs survive. Name is Ho-Chunk for 'duck.' Outflow is Wingra Creek to Lake Monona. Dammed since 1908 (original dam had a wooden lock for pleasure boats); current gravity dam, 8 ft structural height, completed 1930. North shore holds Henry Vilas Zoo, Wingra Park, Wingra Boats livery and Edgewood College. Motor rules: no gas motors on weekends (trolling motor only), weekdays no-wake 5 mph. Late Woodland effigy mounds ring the high ground; the lake was the epicenter of effigy-mound activity and springs and mounds remain sacred to the Ho-Chunk.
landmarks.game_idea: The magic pond. Shallow enough to wade, so it teaches water traversal before Surf. The springs are literal mana/save/heal points feeding a groundwater layer BENEATH the map — an underground aquifer dungeon linking spring mouths, where dead springs are blocked passages you restore one at a time to bring the lake back. Effigy mounds on the ridge are a shape-language puzzle read only from above. No-motor rule = enforced silent traversal, paddle only, stealth zone.

landmarks.name: Tenney Park Lock and Dam
landmarks.character: The keystone of the whole system. Largest of the three Yahara locks, on Mendota's east shore along Sherman Ave between Filene Park and Tenney Beach. It is what makes Mendota (850 ft) and Monona (845 ft) navigable as one system, and it sets Monona's water level. Staffed by an attendant during posted hours; a daily or annual Tenney Lock Permit is required and shown to the attendant; off-hours passage needs 48 hours' notice to Dane County Parks. Small craft can portage around it, or carry ~100 ft over to the Tenney Park lagoon and loop the island. Below it the Yahara runs about a mile as a no-wake canal across the isthmus.
landmarks.game_idea: The literal gate between the two seas — a lock is a fantastic dungeon-as-machine. Water rises and falls in a chamber while you stand in it: a timed vertical puzzle where the chamber IS the elevator. Permit-and-attendant gives you a canonical toll NPC and a 'come back during operating hours' time gate. The 48-hour off-hours request is a perfect sidequest. And it is the single point of control for Monona's water level — capture the lock, command the lake.

landmarks.name: The Yahara Isthmus Canal
landmarks.character: For roughly one mile between Mendota and Monona the Yahara is essentially a canal, no-wake, threading Madison's near-east side under a dense stack of crossings: Sherman Avenue, East Johnson, two rail bridges (one converted to a bike-ped path), East Washington, East Main, two more rail bridges (one bike-ped), the Williamson/Winnebago span, a pedestrian-bicycle bridge at Jenifer Street, and Rutledge Street. Mickey's Tavern sits at the Willy Street bridge. The annual Paddle and Portage race carries boats overland across the isthmus through Tenney Park to reach it, then paddles down to Olbrich Park.
landmarks.game_idea: A corridor level with a rhythm built in — ten crossings in one mile is a metronome of ducking, timing, and overhead threats. Bridges are enemy perches, ambush points and shortcuts (the two bike-ped rail conversions are the ones you can climb onto). No-wake means enforced slow movement: a stealth/pursuit sequence where speed is denied. Portage as a mechanic — carry your boat overland — is the game's answer to 'why can't I just sail everywhere.'

landmarks.name: Wingra Creek
landmarks.character: The link from Lake Wingra down to Monona Bay: about an hour of relaxed paddling with almost no current, a green corridor of trees and brush screening the city, running between Goodman and Quann Parks, under three railroad bridges and John Nolen Drive before opening onto Lake Monona with Olin-Turville Park to the right and the downtown skyline to the left. Portage facilities at the Wingra dam let you move between lake and creek. Best paddled early in the season — weed growth turns it into an adventure by late summer.
landmarks.game_idea: A seasonal one-way channel. Early game it is an open shortcut; later in the in-game year weed growth chokes it into a Cut-required maze. Low current means you paddle both directions, so it is a true two-way link, unlike a waterfall. The tunnel-like railroad and highway underpasses are dark rooms needing a light source. The reveal at the mouth — screening brush drops away and the Capitol skyline fills the screen — is a free cinematic moment.

landmarks.name: Memorial Union Terrace & the Lakeshore Path
landmarks.character: The social heart of Mendota's south shore and the eastern trailhead of the walkable belt. The Lakeshore Path is two joined trails — the Howard Temin Path (southeast, named for the Nobel laureate who biked it daily) and the Lake Mendota Path (northwest) — running about 4 miles between Observatory Hill and Frautschi Point, curling around University Bay and out to Picnic Point, past Willow Beach and University Bay Marsh. There are 4.3 miles of continuous walkable shoreline from Muir Woods at Park Street west to Wally Bauman Woods near Shorewood Hills. Home to the Hoofer Sailing Club (founded 1939, one of the largest collegiate fleets in the US).
landmarks.game_idea: The hub town's waterfront: quest board, boat rental, sailing school where the player is taught the wind mechanic, and the safe-return point. The 4.3 miles of continuous public shore is your one guaranteed-walkable arc — everything else on Mendota is private and blocked, which makes shoreline access itself a resource the player collects. Hoofers is the trainer NPC that unlocks Surf.

landmarks.name: Monona Terrace & Law Park
landmarks.character: The Frank Lloyd Wright-designed convention center built out over Lake Monona's north shore, with a public rooftop. Access to the waterfront strip here is limited to the far east and west ends plus a midpoint connection through Monona Terrace itself — a pinch in the shoreline path. The Law Park fishing pier is out for the 2026 season during John Nolen Drive reconstruction and returns further north in 2027. A master plan will run a continuous waterfront park from Law Park to Olin Park with separated pedestrian, cycling and running paths along the John Nolen causeway.
landmarks.game_idea: A building that IS the bridge — the only way along this shore is through the structure, so the interior is a mandatory transit dungeon with a rooftop vista that unlocks the fast-travel map of Monona. Three access points only (east, west, middle) makes it a genuine chokepoint puzzle. The missing fishing pier is a nice 'come back next year / next chapter' state change: an NPC waiting for a pier that does not exist yet.

landmarks.name: Olbrich Park & the Starkweather Creek mouth
landmarks.character: On Madison's east side along Lake Monona, next to Olbrich Botanical Gardens. Lake access at the mouth of Starkweather Creek — the largest single source of phosphorus entering Monona after the river. Requires a Lake Access Permit; Rutabaga Paddlesports rents there seasonally. It is the finish line of the Paddle and Portage. Just west, past Yahara Place Park, the public can walk the Monona shore until the property line near Dunning Street — where public access simply stops.
landmarks.game_idea: The east-shore launch point and a pollution-source dungeon: follow the phosphorus upstream into Starkweather to find and shut down what is feeding the algal blooms, which visibly clears the lake's water shader afterward. The hard stop at Dunning Street where public shoreline ends is a great physical 'invisible wall' with an in-world reason — a property line, not level geometry — and a quest to open it.

landmarks.name: Lake Waubesa
landmarks.character: Third lake down the chain, ~2,074 acres, max depth 38 ft, fed and drained by the Yahara plus Nine Springs wastewater effluent. Ho-Chunk name Sahu Xetera, 'Tall Reed Lake' — the Waubesa Wetlands on its south end are the defining feature. Reached from Monona through Upper Mud Lake. Babcock County Park in McFarland holds the second lock, which is free but may close during low-water periods when lakes are at summer minimum; a portage is provided. State-record yellow bass (16.1 in, 2 lb 12 oz) caught here in 2013.
landmarks.game_idea: The reed-maze lake: tall-reed wetlands as a Cut-navigable labyrinth where sightlines drop to zero and the minimap becomes unreliable. Babcock Lock being free but conditionally closed is a superb soft gate — the passage exists, but only when water is high, so the chain's lower half opens and closes with the season. Nine Springs effluent gives you a legitimate corrupted-inflow zone.

landmarks.name: Lake Kegonsa & LaFollette Lock
landmarks.character: Last lake of the four, ~3,200 acres, max depth 32 ft, elevation 843 ft. Hocak name Nasakucitera, 'Hard Maple Grove Lake.' Glacially formed ~12,000 years ago in the Wisconsin glaciation. In 1829 a documented Ho-Chunk camp at the Yahara outlet held about 106 people in 11 structures. Lake Kegonsa State Park (343 acres, established 1962, opened 1966) is on the northeast shore. LaFollette County Park near Stoughton holds the third and final lock — free, portage provided, may close at low water. Between Babcock and LaFollette the route is ~6.5 mi and about 90% lake paddling, with a brief river section holding a riffle or two, a short boulder garden, and remnants of Native American fish weirs near the old Dyreson Road truss bridge.
landmarks.game_idea: The end of the chain and the reward for completing all three locks. The stone fish weirs near Dyreson Road are a ready-made ancient-mechanism puzzle: a thousand-year-old device for funneling fish, reusable as a current-redirection gate. The boulder garden is the chain's only whitewater — a short skill-check rapids run. Beyond LaFollette the Yahara keeps going 20+ miles to the Rock River: the map's edge, and the sequel hook.

landmarks.name: Cherokee Marsh
landmarks.character: The Yahara's entry into Lake Mendota at the far north — the river's upper wetland before it becomes lake. The paddle from Cherokee Marsh to Tenney Lock is 5.75 miles, crossing Mendota's northeast shore past Governor's Island and its sandstone outcrop, along the least developed stretch of the whole chain.
landmarks.game_idea: The wild north edge, deliberately empty and quiet as contrast to the built-up isthmus. This is where the river narrows into the map boundary — an upstream trickle you follow to a source. A 5.75-mile open crossing to reach the lock makes it the longest single traversal on Mendota: the endurance run that proves the player has mastered Surf and the wind system.

landmarks.name: Vilas Park & Wingra Boats
landmarks.character: Lake Wingra's north shore: Henry Vilas Park and Vilas Park Beach, the Henry Vilas Zoo, Wingra Park, and Wingra Boats livery renting rowboats, canoes, pedal boats, kayaks, watermats and stand-up paddleboards. Edgewood College adjoins. Most of Wingra's shoreline is publicly accessible — unusually, this small lake is the MOST walkable of the group, while the biggest lake is the least.
landmarks.game_idea: The rental hub and the game's tool shed — every traversal item is available here first, cheaply, on the safest water. A free zoo next to the boat livery hands you a creature-collection nexus without contrivance. Because Wingra's whole 4-mile shore is walkable, it is the one lake you can fully circumnavigate on foot at hour one, which teaches the player what 'lapping a lake' costs before you ask them to consider lapping Mendota's 22 miles.

notes:
TRAVERSAL LAYER — a Surf/Whirlpool/Waterfall design over the Yahara chain.

The single best design fact here: this is a real, plumbed, gated water system with an actual hierarchy, and it already behaves like a Zelda/Pokemon traversal ladder. Elevations descend 850 ft (Mendota) -> 845 ft (Monona) -> Waubesa -> 843 ft (Kegonsa), and three real locks control passage between them. You do not need to invent gating; the county already built it.

SURF (open-water movement). Three tiers of water, well differentiated:
- Tier 1, Lake Wingra: 14 ft max, 4 mi of nearly all-public shoreline, no gas motors on weekends and 5 mph no-wake weekdays. Safe, slow, shallow, teaching water.
- Tier 2, Lake Monona: 3,274 acres, 74 ft max, 13 mi shore but only ~40% public. Structured, urban, chokepointed by causeways.
- Tier 3, Lake Mendota: 9,740 acres, 83 ft max, 21.6 mi shore, 5.6 x 4.1 mi of open water with serious fetch. Gate this behind wind mastery. Model wind as a directional field on the long axis — with-wind is fast, into-wind requires tacking. This is real (Hoofers, founded 1939, and Mendota Yacht Club, 1903, race here) and it turns open water into a skill space instead of a flat plane.

WATERFALL / vertical passage = THE LOCKS. Three of them, and they are dungeon machines already:
- Tenney Lock (Mendota->isthmus canal, 43.09497 / -89.37074): largest, staffed by an attendant, requires a paid daily or annual permit, operates only on posted hours, and off-hours passage needs 48 hours' notice. That is a toll NPC, a time gate, and a sidequest in one real institution. It also SETS LAKE MONONA'S WATER LEVEL — make that a player-controllable global.
- Babcock Lock (Waubesa, Babcock County Park, 43.00678 / -89.30415): free, but may close during low-water summer minimum. A conditional gate that opens and shuts with the season.
- LaFollette Lock (Kegonsa, near Stoughton): free, same low-water conditionality.
All three provide a portage for small watercraft — so the lock is the fast path and portage is the always-available slow path. That is exactly the shape of a good optional shortcut.

WHIRLPOOL / warp nodes: use the peninsula tips and the deep hole. Picnic Point's tip (1 mi out into the lake) launching to Governor's Island across open water is the flagship crossing. The Mendota deep hole (83 ft, between Picnic Point and Maple Bluff) is the one dive-only entrance.

PORTAGE as a first-class verb. The real Paddle and Portage race carries boats overland across the isthmus through Tenney Park. Bake this in: the player can always carry the boat, slowly and vulnerably, when the lock is shut. It answers "why can't I sail everywhere" with a cost rather than a wall.

WALKABILITY — this is the sharpest asymmetry in the whole map and should drive level design:
- Lake Wingra: mostly public shoreline, ~4 mi, fully lappable on foot. Smallest lake, most walkable.
- Lake Mendota: 21.6 mi of shore but only 4.3 mi of continuous public shoreline (Muir Woods at Park St west to Wally Bauman Woods near Shorewood Hills), plus the 4-mi Lakeshore Path (Howard Temin Path + Lake Mendota Path, Observatory Hill to Frautschi Point) and the 300-acre Lakeshore Nature Preserve covering 4 mi of the south shore. The rest is private. Biggest lake, least walkable.
- Lake Monona: 13 mi shore, ~40% publicly owned; the signed Lake Monona Loop is ~13 mi using paths and low-traffic streets, and the Capital City Trail (20+ mi) runs the John Nolen causeway. Public access hard-stops at a property line near Dunning Street past Yahara Place Park — an in-world invisible wall with an actual reason.
Design consequence: shoreline access is itself a collectible resource. The player unlocks walkable segments the way they'd unlock map regions.

BRIDGES AND CHOKEPOINTS. The one-mile isthmus canal carries about ten crossings: Sherman Ave, E. Johnson, two rail bridges (one bike-ped conversion), E. Washington, E. Main, two more rail bridges (one bike-ped), Williamson/Winnebago, a pedestrian bridge at Jenifer St, and Rutledge St. Ten crossings in one mile is a built-in rhythm section. Monona Bay is nearly sealed from Monona by the John Nolen causeway and rail embankment — a wall with one gap. Monona Terrace allows shoreline passage at only three points (far east, far west, and through the building itself).

WINTER ICE — the strongest structural idea available. Mendota's median ice duration is 105 days, average freeze around Dec 20, records kept since 1852-53. Longest ever: 161 days (1880-81). Shortest: about three weeks (2001-02). The lake has lost roughly six weeks of ice cover across the record. Monona freezes ~107 days; Wingra ~120 days (shallowest freezes longest and hardest).
Use this as a seasonal map-flip: in winter the entire lake surface becomes walkable overworld, Surf is disabled, and the locks are irrelevant because you walk over them. Real winter activity supports the fiction — iceboating with the Four Lakes Ice Yacht Club (Madison has one of the world's largest clubs; boats hit 60-100 mph), ice fishing, hockey rinks built on the lake, snowkiting, cross-country skiing, and the Clean Lakes Alliance Frozen Assets festival at the Edgewater. Iceboats are a legitimate high-speed winter traversal item that uses the SAME wind system as summer sailing — one mechanic, two seasons. Make ice thickness a variable: thin ice near inflows and springs, and Wingra (shallow, 120 days) safe long before Mendota (deep, 105 days) is.

FISHING as a systems layer. Mendota holds ~34 species: walleye, musky, northern pike, white bass, yellow perch, largemouth and smallmouth bass. Monona adds lake sturgeon and heavy panfish. Waubesa produced a state-record yellow bass (2013). Depth and season should govern the catch table: shallow weedy Wingra vs. Mendota's 83-ft deep hole should not yield the same list.

ECOLOGICAL STATE as a progress meter. All these lakes are eutrophic from agricultural and urban runoff; Mendota flipped from mesotrophic starting in the late 1800s. Starkweather Creek is Monona's largest phosphorus source after the river. Beach closures run 40-60+ days a summer from cyanobacteria and E. coli. Zebra mussels have reproduced in Mendota since 2015 and filter algae but not cyanobacteria, worsening nearshore blooms. Only a fraction of Lake Wingra's historic springs survive. Every one of these is a restorable world-state: clear the water, reopen the beaches, restore the springs, and change the water shader and the fish tables as visible proof.

CULTURAL LAYER — handle with care and it is the richest material on the map. Ho-Chunk names are the true names: Mendota is Waaksikhomikra, Monona is Tchee-ho-bo-kee-xa-te-la ('Teepee Lake'), Wingra means 'duck', Waubesa is Sahu Xetera ('Tall Reed Lake'), Kegonsa is Nasakucitera ('Hard Maple Grove Lake'). Late Woodland effigy mounds ring Lake Wingra, which was the epicenter of mound-building; three burial mounds sit atop Eagle Heights Woods. Picnic Point shows at least 12,000 years of habitation. In 2019 Dane County renamed Squaw Bay to Wicawak Bay (Ho-Chunk for muskrat) at the Ho-Chunk Nation's request, first made in 2005. Springs and mounds remain sacred sites. Treat mounds as inviolable landmarks and vantage points, never as loot containers — and the renaming makes an excellent quest about maps being wrong and names being restored.

CAUTION ON COORDINATES: every approx_lat/approx_lon above came from Wikipedia infoboxes or OpenStreetMap Nominatim lookups. Wicawak Bay has no coordinate given — it is not yet indexed in OSM under the new name and I would not guess it; the isthmus canal and Wingra Creek midpoints are marked "rough" because they are line features I estimated from described endpoints rather than looked up as points. Also note two source conflicts worth knowing: Lake Monona's max depth is given as 74 ft by Wikipedia but 64 ft by Clean Lakes Alliance, and Mendota's surface area as 9,740 acres (Wikipedia) vs 9,842 acres (Clean Lakes Alliance). Mendota's median freeze date is variously reported as ~Dec 20 and Jan 1 depending on whether the source means initial closing or full sustained ice.

area: Johto region — Pokémon Gold/Silver (Game Boy Color, Gen II), the 8-badge Johto gym arc from New Bark Town to Blackthorn City. Johto is explicitly modelled on Japan's Kansai region (Bulbapedia); several gym cities have documented real-world analogues, which is why approximate coordinates are given for 7 of the 8 gyms. Those coordinates locate the REAL-WORLD INSPIRATION, not the fictional city — they are useful as a shape/spacing reference for a map, not as canonical geography.
biomes: Rural grassland and hedgerow farmland (Routes 29/30/31, 38/39, Moomoo Farm)
Historic temple town / ruins (Violet City, Sprout Tower, Ruins of Alph)
Cave and underground systems (Dark Cave, Union Cave, Slowpoke Well, Mt. Mortar)
Dense old-growth forest (Ilex Forest)
Dense metropolis with subterranean level (Goldenrod City, Goldenrod Underground)
Manicured park / meadow (National Park)
Historic spiritual city with ruined and standing towers (Ecruteak City, Burned Tower, Tin/Bell Tower)
Port coast and lighthouse headland (Olivine City, Route 40)
Open ocean and island archipelago with whirlpools (Route 41, Whirl Islands, Cianwood beach)
Lake and freshwater wetland (Lake of Rage, the lakes bisecting Routes 42 and 44)
Alpine snowfield and glacier cave (Mahogany Town, Ice Path)
Volcanic crater / rocky dragon highland (Blackthorn City, Dragon's Den, Route 45)

landmarks.name: Gym 1 — Violet City Gym (Falkner, Flying, Zephyr Badge)
landmarks.character: ACE: Pidgeotto Lv 9 (team: Pidgey Lv 7, Pidgeotto Lv 9 — 2 Pokémon). Reward TM31 Mud-Slap. WILD BAND ON APPROACH: Lv 2-7 — Route 29 Lv 2-4, Route 30 Lv 2-5, Route 31 Lv 2-6, Dark Cave Lv 2-6, Sprout Tower Bellsprout Lv 3-6. GATE UNLOCKED: Zephyr Badge permits Flash outside battle (HM05 is won separately, from Elder Li at the top of Sprout Tower) and raises traded-Pokémon obedience to Lv 20; it also boosts Attack. This is the softest gate in the game — Flash reveals dark caves (Dark Cave, Union Cave B2F) but blocks no critical path. POSITION: roughly the first 10-12% of the Johto arc, 1-2 hours in. Pre-gym dungeon Sprout Tower front-loads Bellsprout so the player's starter is force-taught the type chart before the gym. Real-world basis: Nara, the Nara-period capital, which is why the city is temple-and-pagoda themed.
landmarks.game_idea: Make the FIRST boss the lowest-level boss you will ever ship and give its badge a non-blocking reward. Falkner at Lv 9 is only ~2-3 levels above the local wild ceiling — the player can beat him with the starter alone and no grinding. Pair every gym with a small themed dungeon in the same town whose enemies preview the gym's weakness, and separate the KEY (the HM item, found in that dungeon) from the PERMISSION (the badge) so the player holds a locked tool for a few minutes before it turns on.

landmarks.name: Gym 2 — Azalea Town Gym (Bugsy, Bug, Hive Badge)
landmarks.character: ACE: Scyther Lv 16 (team: Metapod Lv 14, Kakuna Lv 14, Scyther Lv 16 — 3 Pokémon). Reward TM49 Fury Cutter. WILD BAND: Lv 4-10 — Route 32 Lv 4-8, Union Cave 1F Lv 4-7 and B1F Lv 6-9, Slowpoke Well Lv 5-10. GATE UNLOCKED: Hive Badge permits Cut outside battle; HM01 Cut is given by the charcoal maker's son in Ilex Forest after you retrieve his runaway Farfetch'd. This is the game's FIRST hard traversal gate — a cuttable tree in Ilex Forest is the only road west, so Cut opens the entire western half of Johto. Obedience to Lv 30. PRECONDITION: Team Rocket occupies Slowpoke Well; you must beat the Grunts and Proton and free the Slowpoke before the story advances. POSITION: ~25% of the arc. Real-world basis: Minabe, Wakayama, famous for binchōtan charcoal — hence the Charcoal Kiln and Kurt's Apricorn Poké Balls.
landmarks.game_idea: Put your first real traversal lock (Cut) on badge 2, not badge 1 — the player should be free to wander for one gym before the map starts issuing keys. Wrap the badge in a villain-faction sidequest (Slowpoke Well) so the gym is not the only reason to be in town, and hide the HM in the dungeon PAST the gym so acquiring the tool and acquiring the licence are two separate beats.

landmarks.name: Gym 3 — Goldenrod City Gym (Whitney, Normal, Plain Badge)
landmarks.character: ACE: Miltank Lv 20 (team: Clefairy Lv 18, Miltank Lv 20 — 2 Pokémon). Reward TM45 Attract. WILD BAND: Lv 5-13 — Ilex Forest Lv 5-7, Route 34 Lv 10-13. GATE UNLOCKED: Plain Badge permits Strength outside battle (HM04 is found much later, on Route 42 near Mt. Mortar) and boosts Speed; narratively it also unblocks the north exit toward Route 35 / National Park. POSITION: ~35% of the arc. Notorious as the game's real difficulty spike: Miltank runs Rollout + Attract + Milk Drink and outclasses a Lv 20 party by a wide margin, and the badge is not handed over until you talk to Whitney a second time after her tantrum. Goldenrod is the region's content hub — Department Store, Game Corner, Radio Tower, Underground, Bike Shop, Name Rater, Bill's house (free Eevee). Real-world basis: Osaka.
landmarks.game_idea: Place your one deliberate difficulty spike at the one-third mark, in your richest city, where a losing player has the most alternatives (shops, side content, a bike, free party members) to solve it without leaving the area. Also: it is fine to grant a movement permission (Strength) five hours before the player finds the tool that uses it — the delayed payoff makes a mid-game route feel like a reward rather than a chore.

landmarks.name: Gym 4 — Ecruteak City Gym (Morty, Ghost, Fog Badge)
landmarks.character: ACE: Gengar Lv 25 (team: Gastly Lv 21, Haunter Lv 21, Haunter Lv 23, Gengar Lv 25 — 4 Pokémon, the first full-size boss team). Reward TM34 Shadow Ball. WILD BAND: Lv 10-16 — Route 35 Lv 10-14, National Park Lv 10-14, Route 36 Lv 12-15, Route 37 Lv 13-16; plus the scripted Lv 20 Sudowoodo that blocks Route 36 until you bring the SquirtBottle. GATE UNLOCKED: Fog Badge permits Surf outside battle — the single largest map unlock in the game. HM03 Surf is given at the Dance Theater after you beat all five Kimono Girls. The badge also opens the Barrier Station to Tin/Bell Tower and is required to head west toward Route 38 and Olivine. Obedience to Lv 50. POSITION: the exact structural midpoint, ~45% of the arc. Ecruteak is the hub node: Burned Tower here releases the roaming legendary beasts. Real-world basis: Kyoto, Japan's cultural capital.
landmarks.game_idea: Reserve the water/traversal skill that converts your map from a corridor into an open field for the exact midpoint, and make the midpoint city a HUB rather than a stop — every subsequent branch should radiate from it. Give this boss your first four-unit team so the fight physically feels like a chapter break. Bonus trick worth stealing: gym 3 is Normal and gym 4 is Ghost, a mutual-immunity pair placed back to back, so the rules lesson lands the moment the player has just enough type literacy to be surprised by it.

landmarks.name: Gym 5 — Cianwood City Gym (Chuck, Fighting, Storm Badge)
landmarks.character: ACE: Poliwrath Lv 30 (team: Primeape Lv 27, Poliwrath Lv 30 — 2 Pokémon). Reward TM01 DynamicPunch. WILD BAND: Lv 13-24 — Route 38 Lv 13-16, Route 39 Lv 15-20, then a long Surf across Routes 40/41 at Lv 20-24 (Tentacool, Tentacruel, Mantine). GATE UNLOCKED: Storm Badge permits Fly outside battle; HM02 Fly is handed over by Chuck's wife standing outside the gym the moment you win. Obedience to Lv 70. Fly turns the whole region into a fast-travel graph. POSITION: ~55-60%, but reached OUT OF CITY ORDER — Cianwood sits on the far western edge, reachable only by surfing from Olivine, and the player is sent there on Jasmine's SecretPotion errand. Real-world basis: Naruto, Tokushima; the Whirl Islands between Olivine and Cianwood are the Naruto Strait whirlpools.
landmarks.game_idea: Grant fast travel at the point of MAXIMUM distance from home, immediately after the longest one-way traversal in the game. The player earns Fly on a peninsula they can only reach by water, so the reward is felt as relief rather than convenience. Structurally: a gym you reach by errand rather than by road is the cheapest way to make a linear map feel non-linear.

landmarks.name: Gym 6 — Olivine City Gym (Jasmine, Steel, Mineral Badge)
landmarks.character: ACE: Steelix Lv 35 (team: Magnemite Lv 30, Magnemite Lv 30, Steelix Lv 35 — 3 Pokémon). Reward TM23 Iron Tail. Highest ace level of the first seven gyms — HIGHER than the gym that follows it. WILD BAND: the same Lv 13-24 approach band as Chuck (Routes 38/39 and the sea Routes 40/41), because both gyms hang off the same lobe. GATE UNLOCKED: NOTHING. The Mineral Badge is the only Johto badge that authorises no field move; it grants a Defense boost and an obedience step. STRUCTURE: you arrive in Olivine and find Jasmine in the Lighthouse, a dead-end dungeon whose only output is a quest flag — her Ampharos 'Amphy' is sick and she refuses to battle. You must Surf to Cianwood, buy the SecretPotion at the Pharmacy, and return. POSITION: ~60-65%. Steel and Dark were both new in Gen II; Steel gets the gym, Dark never gets one anywhere in the 16-badge game. Real-world basis: Kobe, a port city.
landmarks.game_idea: Build one 'refused boss': introduce a boss who will not fight until the player completes an errand elsewhere, and make that errand contain ANOTHER boss. This single move converts two sequential gyms into a lobe hanging off one map node, gives the player order freedom, and justifies a long round trip. Also worth copying: deliberately make one badge in eight a pure stat/permission reward with no key attached, so the badge economy is not a mechanical checklist.

landmarks.name: Gym 7 — Mahogany Town Gym (Pryce, Ice, Glacier Badge)
landmarks.character: ACE: Piloswine Lv 31 (team: Seel Lv 27, Dewgong Lv 29, Piloswine Lv 31 — 3 Pokémon). Reward TM16 Icy Wind. NOTE THE REGRESSION: the ace level DROPS from Jasmine's 35 to 31 — the only backward step in the whole curve. WILD BAND: Lv 13-19 — Route 42 Lv 13-17, Route 43 Lv 15-17, Lake of Rage Magikarp/Gyarados Lv 10-19, plus the scripted red Gyarados at Lv 30. GATE UNLOCKED: Glacier Badge permits Whirlpool outside battle; HM06 Whirlpool is given by Lance inside the Team Rocket Hideout beneath the town. Boosts Sp. Attack and Sp. Defense. Whirlpool is primarily an OPTIONAL-CONTENT key: it opens the four Whirl Islands (Lugia) and the sea passage on Route 41, plus Route 27 toward Kanto. PRECONDITION: Pryce refuses to battle until the red Gyarados at Lake of Rage is dealt with and Team Rocket's Mahogany HQ is cleared; the eastern exit is separately blocked by the RageCandyBar seller until you hold seven badges. POSITION: ~75% of the arc. The gym interior is an ice-sliding maze — the first gym whose ROOM is a puzzle. Real-world basis: Kōka, Shiga, historic home of the Kōga-ryū ninja school.
landmarks.game_idea: This is the load-bearing lesson for non-linear design: when you let players reach two bosses in either order, you must tune the later-reachable one to the WEAKER possible party, and accept a flat or negative difficulty slope there. Pryce is under-levelled on purpose because the Olivine lobe may have over-levelled the player. Second rule: gate a late boss behind a faction dungeon rather than a level check — the player is stopped by narrative permission, which never feels like grinding. Third: by gym 7, make the boss's ROOM a puzzle, not just the boss.

landmarks.name: Gym 8 — Blackthorn City Gym (Clair, Dragon, Rising Badge)
landmarks.character: ACE: Kingdra Lv 40 (team: Dragonair Lv 37, Dragonair Lv 37, Dragonair Lv 37, Kingdra Lv 40 — 4 Pokémon, the second full-size boss team). Reward TM24 DragonBreath. Biggest single jump in the game: +9 levels over Pryce. WILD BAND: Lv 20-27 — Route 44 Lv 22-26, Ice Path Lv 20-23 (Jynx, Swinub, Delibird, Golbat), Route 45 Lv 20-27 (Graveler, Gligar, Teddiursa, Phanpy). GATE UNLOCKED: Rising Badge permits Waterfall outside battle; HM07 Waterfall is found lying inside the Ice Path, BEFORE you have the badge to use it. Obedience to Lv 100. Waterfall is the final movement key — it opens Victory Road, Mt. Silver and the route to Kanto, i.e. the entire second half of the game. PRECONDITIONS AND APPROACH: reaching Blackthorn requires Route 44 (bisected by lakes, needs Surf and Cut) and the Ice Path (needs Strength for a boulder-into-hole puzzle — cashing in the badge-3 permission five gyms later). After you beat Clair she REFUSES the badge; you must enter Dragon's Den behind the gym and pass the Elder's quiz on how you treat your Pokémon to receive it, plus a Dratini. The Goldenrod Radio Tower Rocket takeover sits between Pryce and Clair. POSITION: ~90% of the arc; the Elite Four follow at Lv 40-50. Bulbapedia gives no documented real-world basis for Blackthorn, so no coordinate is offered — the field is present only to keep the record shape consistent.
landmarks.game_idea: End the arc with a boss who requires every traversal tool you have shipped — the road to Clair consumes Surf, Cut and Strength in sequence — so the final approach is a de facto exam on the whole gating system. Give the last boss the largest level jump AND a second-phase gate (Clair withholding the badge until the Dragon's Den quiz) so the finale is two beats, not one. And drop the final HM in the dungeon just BEFORE the boss who licenses it: the player carries Waterfall unusable for twenty minutes, which makes the badge land as a key turning.

notes:
EXTRACTED DESIGN RULES — Johto's 8-gym arc as a balance benchmark.

1) TYPE-COVERAGE SPREAD (what 8 bosses are "about")
Order: Flying, Bug, Normal, Ghost, Fighting, Steel, Ice, Dragon — 8 of Gen II's 17 types.
- The three starter types (Fire, Water, Grass) are DELIBERATELY absent from all 8 Johto gyms. No starter choice is punished or privileged by gym order. Kanto's 8 badges (post-game) then cover Rock, Water, Electric, Grass, Poison, Psychic, Fire, Ground — the near-exact complement, so the 16-badge game touches 16 of 17 types. Dark is the only type never given a gym.
- Difficulty of the TYPE tracks position: early gyms are frail, low-BST types (Flying, Bug, Normal) that teach the chart cheaply; late gyms are defensive/rare types (Steel, Ice, Dragon). Steel was brand new in Gen II and gets a gym as a showcase.
- No two adjacent gyms share an answer. The counter you need rotates every time: Rock/Electric → Fire/Flying/Rock → Fighting → Dark/Ghost → Flying/Psychic → Fire/Fighting/Ground → Fire/Steel/Rock → Ice/Dragon. A single over-levelled sweeper cannot carry two gyms in a row.
- The Normal (3) → Ghost (4) adjacency is a mutual-immunity pair placed back to back, teaching the immunity rule exactly when the player has two gyms of chart literacy.

2) LEVEL CURVE SLOPE
Ace levels: 9, 16, 20, 25, 30, 35, 31, 40. Deltas: +7, +4, +5, +5, +5, −4, +9.
- Total span 31 levels over 8 bosses; mean +4.4/gym, but the shape is: one steep opening jump (9→16, +78% relative), then a metronomic +5 per gym through gyms 2-6, one deliberate −4 regression at gym 7, then a +9 finale.
- The gym ace consistently sits 3-6 levels ABOVE the top of the wild band the player just walked through (e.g. Bugsy 16 vs a Lv 4-10 band + trainers; Morty 25 vs a Lv 10-16 band; Clair 40 vs a Lv 20-27 band). The boss is the local ceiling, never a wall you must grind past by more than a few levels — the gap widens slightly toward the end (Clair is ~13 over the top of Route 45) to force one real party-building pass before the Elite Four.
- Boss team SIZE is not monotone: 2, 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 3, 4. The two four-unit teams land on gym 4 (midpoint) and gym 8 (finale) — team size is used as a chapter-break signal, not as a difficulty dial.
- Wild-band curve is roughly Lv 2-7 → 4-10 → 5-13 → 10-16 → 13-24 → 13-24 → 13-19 → 20-27. Note it is NOT monotone either: the sea routes (20-24) spike early because Surf opens deep water, and the Mahogany approach dips back to 13-19. The game accepts a jagged wild curve as the price of open traversal.

3) HOW BADGES GATE MOVEMENT (the core loop)
Every badge is a PERMISSION; the HM is a separate ITEM hidden in the world. You need both.
- Zephyr (1) → Flash. HM05 in Sprout Tower. Visibility only; softest gate.
- Hive (2) → Cut. HM01 in Ilex Forest (Farfetch'd errand). First hard traversal gate — opens the entire west.
- Plain (3) → Strength. HM04 on Route 42. Permission granted long before the tool is found; cashed in at the Ice Path five gyms later.
- Fog (4) → Surf. HM03 from the Dance Theater. The largest single map unlock; converts corridor to open field at the midpoint.
- Storm (5) → Fly. HM02 from Chuck's wife. Converts the map into a fast-travel graph, granted at maximum distance from home.
- Mineral (6) → nothing. The one intentionally empty slot.
- Glacier (7) → Whirlpool. HM06 from Lance in the Rocket Hideout. Primarily an OPTIONAL-content key (Whirl Islands/Lugia) plus the Route 27 path to Kanto.
- Rising (8) → Waterfall. HM07 found inside the Ice Path BEFORE the badge exists. Final gate to Victory Road, Mt. Silver and Kanto.
Ratio: 6 of 8 badges unlock a field move; 7 of 8 raise the obedience cap for traded Pokémon (roughly 10 → 20 (Zephyr) → 30 (Hive) → 50 (Fog) → 70 (Storm) → 80 (Mineral) → 100 (Rising) — Gen II steps the cap roughly every second badge in badge-case order). Badges also grant flat stat boosts on a rotation: Attack (Zephyr), Speed (Plain), Defense (Mineral), Sp.Atk+Sp.Def (Glacier).
Three of the seven HMs are placed in the world BEFORE the badge that authorises them (Strength, Whirlpool, Waterfall). Carrying a locked key is a deliberate anticipation device.

4) THE NON-LINEAR OLIVINE / CIANWOOD DETOUR
Ecruteak (gym 4) is the hub. Fog Badge grants Surf; the road west runs Routes 38-39 to Olivine. In Olivine, gym 6's leader Jasmine is found not in her gym but at the top of the Lighthouse — a dead-end dungeon whose only output is a quest flag (Amphy is sick). You then Surf Routes 40-41 (Lv 20-24 water, whirlpool-blocked islands en route) to Cianwood, where you fight gym 5 (Chuck), collect the SecretPotion from the Pharmacy, and receive Fly. You return to Olivine, heal Amphy, and fight gym 6.
Net shape: a 3-4 hour LOBE entered and exited at the same map node, containing two badges, one HM (Fly), the SecretPotion, and later access to the Whirl Islands. Its four functions:
 (a) it breaks the town→gym→town→gym metronome at the exact midpoint;
 (b) it gives real order freedom (Chuck before Jasmine, or backtrack);
 (c) it EARNS Fly by making the return trip genuinely long;
 (d) it explains the Pryce level regression — the game cannot know how over-levelled the lobe left you, so the next boss is tuned down.
Cost, stated plainly: the only broken slope in the game (35 → 31) is the direct price of the only real branch in the game. That trade is the benchmark's clearest lesson.

5) OPTIONAL CONTENT AS PACING VALVE
- Gym-adjacent mini-dungeons that pre-load each gym: Sprout Tower (Violet), Slowpoke Well (Azalea), Burned Tower (Ecruteak), Olivine Lighthouse, Team Rocket Hideout (Mahogany), Dragon's Den (Blackthorn). Several are mandatory story gates rather than true optional content — the villain faction (Team Rocket at Slowpoke Well, Mahogany HQ, and the Goldenrod Radio Tower between gyms 7 and 8) is used three times as a non-level gate.
- Pure optional: Ruins of Alph (Unown, between gyms 1-2), National Park Bug-Catching Contest (real-clock Tue/Thu/Sat, parked between gyms 3-4), Mt. Mortar, Whirl Islands, Dark Cave, Headbutt trees on nearly every route, Kurt's Apricorn Poké Balls, Goldenrod's Game Corner / Department Store / Underground / Bike Shop / free Eevee.
- Ambient, non-blocking objective: the three roaming legendary beasts released at the Burned Tower run underneath the whole second half.
- The governing rule: no optional content sits on the critical path, but EVERY HM the critical path grants opens at least one optional area — so each traversal unlock retroactively re-values the map you already walked. Cut opens shortcut trees everywhere, Surf opens every coast and lake, Whirlpool opens the Whirl Islands, Strength opens boulder rooms, Waterfall opens Mt. Silver.
- Goldenrod is the one gym city that is a destination independent of its gym, and it is placed at the one-third mark — where a player stuck on the game's hardest early fight (Whitney's Miltank) has the most non-combat alternatives to hand.

6) BIOME / ENVIRONMENT COUNT
The 8-gym arc passes through roughly 12 distinct environments (listed in the biomes field), which collapse to 8 headline biomes: grassland, forest, cave, city, coast, open ocean, lake/wetland, snow-mountain/volcanic highland.
Mapped to gyms: G1 grassland + temple town; G2 cave + rural woodland; G3 deep forest + metropolis; G4 park/meadow + historic tower city; G5 open ocean + archipelago beach; G6 port coast + lighthouse headland; G7 lake/wetland + alpine snow; G8 glacier cave + volcanic dragon highland.
That is approximately ONE new signature environment per badge, and no biome is the setting for two consecutive gyms. The arc also alternates settlement scale deliberately: small town (Violet) → small town (Azalea) → metropolis (Goldenrod) → large historic city (Ecruteak) → tiny isolated town (Cianwood) → mid port (Olivine) → tiny town (Mahogany) → mid mountain city (Blackthorn). Scale zig-zags rather than escalating.

7) SUMMARY HEURISTICS FOR YOUR OWN 8-NODE MAP
- Boss level ≈ (top of the local wild band) + 3 to 6; open at +2, finish at +10 or so.
- +5 boss levels per node, one steep opening jump, one four-unit chapter-break boss at the midpoint and one at the end.
- 6 of 8 nodes hand out a traversal key; 1 hands out nothing; split key from permission and occasionally deliver them out of order.
- Exactly one lobe of order-free content, hung off the midpoint hub, containing two bosses — and tune the boss AFTER the lobe to the weaker party.
- One new signature biome per node, never two in a row, with settlement scale zig-zagging.
- Gate late nodes with faction/narrative permission, not level checks.

Research brief on compression ratios, abstraction technique, landmark selection, city shrinking, and turning real transport links into routes and gates.
biomes: Temperate grass route / hedgerow corridor (the default connective tissue)
Dense forest maze (Viridian Forest, Eterna Forest, Glimwood Tangle, Slumbering Weald)
Cave / mine / rail tunnel dungeon (Mt. Moon, Rock Tunnel, Diglett's Cave, Galar Mine, Chargestone Cave)
Mountain pass and alpine spine (Mt. Coronet, Mt. Silver, Twist Mountain, Glaseado Mountain)
Volcanic / ash-fall (Mt. Chimney, Cinnabar's Mt. Mihara analogue, Stark Mountain)
Desert (Desert Resort, Asado Desert, Route 111 sandstorm)
Marsh / wetland reserve (Great Marsh–Kushiro, Safari Zone, Casseroya Lake shallows)
Coastal beach and boardwalk (Humilau, Undella, Slateport, Porto Marinada)
Open sea route with dive layer (Hoenn's southern archipelago, Whirl Islands)
Snowfield / tundra (Snowpoint, Crown Tundra, Montenevera, Icirrus)

Industrial / port / dockside (Vermilion, Motostoke, Hulbury, Canalave, Olivine)
